cards.name: Press-photo frame with caption strip
cards.summary: A news photo sits in a clean white border with a soft shadow, and a dark strip under it carries the caption and the photo credit.
avoid: cropping or retouching the photo's content to fit the frame: crop only, never alter what it shows
a caption strip over the picture's key area: put it below the image, or over a quiet edge
dropping the credit: the strip is where the source and photographer go

effects.name: Stroke
effects.note: On the photo layer: an Inside stroke keeps the corners square (Outside rounds them, as the verified card notes).

effects.name: Drop Shadow
effects.note: Soft lift off the background, falling down-right.

steps.note: One layer style: these 2 effects go into a single layerEffects descriptor (a set replaces the layer's whole style, so separate steps would keep only the last).
Layer > New Fill Layer > Solid Color for the caption strip (#111111), sized to the photo width under its bottom edge (selection set first with doc.selection.select).

steps.name: Color Overlay
steps.note: Optional: keeps the strip colour editable as a style when the strip is a shape layer instead.
Place the photo, draw a rectangle over it at the crop, select both, Make Clipping Mask.
A second rectangle the same size behind it: white fill, or no fill with a 10 pt white stroke, as the border.
On the border rectangle: soft shadow right and down (verified direction for positive values).
Caption strip: a dark rectangle (#111111) under the photo, then the caption and credit as point type on it.

Put the photo inside a rectangle frame (photo.AddToPowerClip(frame, 0)) with a white 0.1 in outline. Untested: PowerClip is a needs_input card with no render test (apply call confirmed: content.AddToPowerClip(frame, 0)).
Soft shadow on the frame, down-right.
Caption strip: Layer.CreateRectangle2 under the frame, Fill.ApplyUniformFill dark grey, then CreateArtisticText for caption and credit.

manual_steps: Write the caption and the credit from the photo's own metadata or the agency's caption; check both before publishing.

cards.name: Quote card with speaker cut-out
cards.summary: A speaker is cut out of their photo and set on a tinted, softened background with a thin white outline, next to their quote in large type with the name and date.
use_for: quote cards for interviews, talks and statements
explainer slides that attribute a claim
avoid: putting words in someone's mouth: use the exact quote, the date and the source
text over the face: keep the quote beside the cut-out, never across it
a hard white outline on a rough automatic cut-out: refine the mask edge first or the outline shows every flaw

steps.note: Duplicate the photo layer: the top copy becomes the cut-out, the bottom copy the background.
Select > Subject on the top copy (verified: selection created; reads the active layer).
Layer Mask > Reveal Selection: non-destructive cut-out (verified mask added).

effects.name: Stroke
effects.note: Thin white outline around the cut-out (follows the mask).

effects.name: Drop Shadow
effects.note: Lifts the speaker off the background, down-right.

steps.note: One layer style: these 2 effects go into a single layerEffects descriptor (a set replaces the layer's whole style, so separate steps would keep only the last).
Bottom copy: blur it into a soft backdrop (verified: smooth haze, detail gone).

steps.name: Color Overlay
steps.note: Also on the bottom copy: a dark tint so white quote type reads on it.
Place a cut-out PNG made in Photoshop (Illustrator cannot cut out a photo by script): soft shadow right and down.
On a copy of the full photo behind it: strong blur for the backdrop (verified render: whole object goes soft).
A dark rectangle over the blurred backdrop in Multiply at 70 % so the quote type reads.
On the placed cut-out PNG (made in Photoshop): a white zero-offset shadow with a small feather draws a soft white rim round the speaker.
On a copy of the full photo behind: Gaussian Blur for the backdrop (verified).
A dark rectangle over the backdrop at transparency 30 (about 70 % opaque) for contrast.

manual_steps: Check the automatic cut-out edge (hair, hands, glasses) and fix the mask by hand before adding the outline.
Verify the quote word for word against the source and add the speaker's name, role and date.

cards.name: Breaking-news strap
cards.summary: A bold lower-third bar: a saturated colour band with a slight gradient and shadow, a contrasting label box at the left and the headline in white.
use_for: lower thirds and chyrons for video explainers
avoid: using 'breaking' styling for old or routine news: label it 'update' or 'explainer'
more than one line of text in the strap: it stops reading at a glance
low-contrast colour pairs: white on saturated red or deep blue, never on yellow

steps.note: Solid Color fill layer for the bar (#C8102E), a full-width rectangle at the lower third.

effects.name: Gradient Overlay
effects.note: Default black-to-white gradient in Overlay at 35 %: the bar lightens toward the top and darkens toward the bottom (verified: white at the top at angle 90).

effects.name: Drop Shadow
effects.note: Shadow straight below the bar (light from the top).

steps.note: One layer style: these 2 effects go into a single layerEffects descriptor (a set replaces the layer's whole style, so separate steps would keep only the last).
Second fill layer for the label box (#FFFFFF) at the left end, with the label in the bar colour.
Optional: Edit > Transform > Skew the label box a few degrees for a dynamic slant.
doc.pathItems.rectangle(...) for the bar and the label box; fill the bar with a red-to-dark-red GradientColor at 90 degrees.
On the bar: shadow straight down (horz 0).
Layer.CreateRectangle2 for the bar and the label box.
Bar: ApplyFountainFill linear at 90 degrees from dark red to red; label: ApplyUniformFill white.
Shadow straight down under the bar.

cards.name: Key-number highlight
cards.summary: The one number that matters is pulled out: big type with a coloured glow or keyline, sitting on a hand-drawn highlighter mark.
use_for: chart call-outs (the latest value, the record)
avoid: highlighting a number without its unit, date and source
glow on light backgrounds: use the keyline or the marker there
several highlighted numbers on one card: highlight one, keep the rest plain

effects.name: Stroke
effects.note: On the number's type layer: dark keyline.

effects.name: Outer Glow
effects.note: Yellow halo, for dark backgrounds (verified: even halo, no offset).

steps.note: One layer style: these 2 effects go into a single layerEffects descriptor (a set replaces the layer's whole style, so separate steps would keep only the last).
Marker: a yellow (#FFE14D) Solid Color fill layer behind the number, a slightly rotated rectangle a bit wider than the figure.
Marker layer in Multiply so it tints like a highlighter pen (render matched the Multiply formula).
On the number (dark background): yellow halo, colour set in the dialog.
Marker: a yellow rectangle behind the number with Scribble: loose back-and-forth marker strokes (verified hand-scribbled fill).
Marker in Multiply.
On the number: one outside contour step in a contrast colour as a keyline (verified sticker / glow look).
Marker: a yellow rectangle behind the number with a smooth, random zipper edge for a hand-drawn wobble. Untested: Random + Smooth was not in the render test.

manual_steps: State the unit, period and source next to the highlighted number.

cards.name: Map highlight callout
cards.summary: One region of a map is lifted out: the rest goes grey and darker, the region keeps its colour with a bright outline and glow, and a label box points to it.
use_for: locating a place in a news explainer
regional data maps (one region in focus)
avoid: map sources you have no right to use: draw from an open-licence map and credit it
disputed borders without a note: say which boundary source the map follows
glow on the region over a busy satellite image: use the outline only

steps.note: Select the region (doc.selection.select with its outline points, or a path), Layer Via Copy: the region becomes its own layer.
Black & White adjustment layer between the base map and the region copy: everything below goes grey (verified greyscale, no tint).
Darken the grey map so the region pops (verified Brightness/Contrast layer).

effects.name: Stroke
effects.note: On the region layer: bright outline.

steps.note: One layer style: these 2 effects go into a single layerEffects descriptor (a set replaces the layer's whole style, so separate steps would keep only the last).
Vector map: set the other regions' opacity to 40 % (pageItem.opacity) or recolour them grey; keep the focus region in full colour on top.
On a copy of the region with no fill and a white stroke: grow it 3 pt so the outline sits just outside the border (verified even growth).
On the same outline: halo (colour set in the dialog).
On the label box: small shadow right and down.
A rectangle over the whole map made into a Tinted Grayscale lens with a neutral grey: the map beneath turns grey (verified monotone in the lens colour).
Duplicate the focus region and bring the copy above the lens so it keeps its colour.
On the region copy: one white outside contour step as the outline.
On the label box: small shadow down-right.

manual_steps: Credit the map data source on the graphic.

cards.name: Before / after split
cards.summary: Two aligned images share one frame: the left half shows 'before', the right half 'after', divided by a crisp line with small labels.
avoid: images not shot from the same angle and scale: align and crop them first or the comparison misleads
colour-grading one side differently from the other: treat both the same
unlabelled halves: always mark which is which and give both dates

steps.note: Put the 'after' layer above 'before' (aligned), then select the right half: doc.selection.select([[w/2,0],[w,0],[w,h],[w/2,h]]).
Layer Mask > Reveal Selection on the 'after' layer: only its right half shows.
Divider: a 4 px white Solid Color fill layer on the centre line.

steps.name: Drop Shadow
steps.note: On the divider: a soft dark edge either side (distance 0) so the line reads on light and dark images. same layerEffects descriptor as any other style on the layer.
Place both images aligned; draw a rectangle over the right half of 'after', select both, Make Clipping Mask.
Divider: a vertical white line (4 pt stroke) on the centre; labels as small boxes.
On the divider: zero-offset shadow for a soft edge.

Clip the 'after' image into a rectangle covering the right half, aligned over 'before'. Untested: PowerClip is a needs_input card with no render test (apply call confirmed: content.AddToPowerClip(frame, 0)).
On the white divider line: zero-offset soft shadow.

manual_steps: Align the two images by hand on fixed landmarks before masking (Photoshop: Edit > Auto-Align Layers helps).

cards.name: Document zoom with highlighter
cards.summary: A page or screenshot is dimmed and softened, one passage is shown enlarged in a framed zoom box, and the key line is marked with a yellow highlighter.
use_for: quoting a report, ruling, filing or web page in an explainer
fact-check graphics that show the source text
avoid: altering the document's words or numbers: zoom and mark only
highlighting out of context: keep the full sentence in the zoom box
personal data visible in the screenshot: blur it first (see the privacy blur recipe)

steps.note: Duplicate the document layer: the bottom copy is the dimmed page, the top becomes the zoom.
Bottom copy: a light blur pushes the page back (verified Gaussian Blur).
Bottom copy: darker (verified Brightness/Contrast).
Top copy: select the passage, Layer Via Copy, then Edit > Free Transform (id 2207) to enlarge it 150-200 %.

effects.name: Stroke
effects.note: On the zoom layer: square white frame (Inside keeps corners square).

steps.note: One layer style: these 2 effects go into a single layerEffects descriptor (a set replaces the layer's whole style, so separate steps would keep only the last).
Highlighter: a yellow (#FFE14D) fill layer over the key line inside the zoom.
Highlighter in Multiply so the text stays black under the yellow (formula-verified).
A rectangle over the passage made into a Magnify lens, 2x (verified: zoomed copy of the art beneath inside the lens, the rest unchanged); move it beside the passage if the zoom should not cover it.
On the lens frame: shadow down-right.
Highlighter: a yellow rectangle under the key line (below the lens in the stack so the lens magnifies it too) at transparency 40.
Dim the rest: a page-size rectangle behind the lens and highlighter as a Brighten lens with a negative rate. Untested: the verified frame used +60 (brighten).
Copy the placed screenshot, clip the copy to the passage (rectangle + Make Clipping Mask), scale it up 150-200 % (pageItem.resize).
White 4 pt stroke rectangle on the zoom; a black rectangle at 40 % opacity over the full page beneath it to dim the rest.
On the zoom group: shadow right and down.
Yellow highlighter rectangle over the key line in Multiply.

manual_steps: Choose the passage and the highlighted line by reading the source; keep the document's title, date and page visible or in the caption.

cards.name: Legibility scrim over a photo
cards.summary: A dark gradient rises from the bottom of a photo so white headline type on it stays readable, with a soft shadow on the type itself.
use_for: headlines and captions set on photos
social cards from a single image
avoid: darkening the subject itself: keep the scrim on the empty part of the frame
a hard-edged band: fade it out, or it reads as a separate box

steps.note: Solid Color fill layer (#000000) above the photo, below the type.

steps.name: Gradient Overlay
steps.note: On the fill layer: gradient from black at the bottom to fully transparent at about 55 % height (stops with an opacity ramp set in the descriptor). same layerEffects descriptor as any other style on the layer.

steps.name: Drop Shadow
steps.note: On the type layer: soft shadow just below the letters.
A rectangle over the bottom of the photo with a black gradient whose top stop has 0 % opacity (gradientStop.opacity), rotated so it fades upward.
The scrim in Multiply keeps the photo's colours under it.
On the type: soft shadow straight down.
A black rectangle over the bottom half of the photo.
Linear fountain transparency from opaque at the bottom to clear at the top (verified linear fade; angle 90 runs it vertically, swap Start / End if it fades the wrong way).
On the text: soft shadow just below.

cards.name: Privacy blur or pixelation
cards.summary: Faces of bystanders, number plates, addresses or personal details in a photo or screenshot are pixelated or blurred beyond recognition and the result is flattened so the original cannot be recovered.
use_for: protecting bystanders, minors and private individuals in news photos
avoid: light blur or small mosaic cells: faces and text can be recovered; use cells at least a quarter of the face width
live, reversible effects in the delivered file (smart filters, Illustrator effects, CorelDRAW lenses): flatten or rasterise before export
forgetting the metadata: strip location and camera data on export

steps.note: Select each area to hide (doc.selection.select with its corners), a little larger than the face or text.
Filter > Pixelate > Mosaic: square blocks of one averaged colour (verified). Scale the cell to the area: 20-40 px on a face.
Then a blur over the same selection removes the block edges that can be de-pixelated.
Layer > Flatten Image before export so no unblurred layer or smart object survives.
Copy the placed image and clip the copy to the area to hide.
Strong blur on the clipped copy (verified: whole object goes soft).
Object > Rasterize the image together with the blurred copy (doc.rasterize(...)): the live effect would otherwise keep the original pixels in the file.
On a cropped copy of the area (a separate bitmap over the original): Pixelate with large square cells (verified with Width 40; the script dropped Mode and Height, so only Square mode applies).
Convert to Bitmap of the photo plus the pixelated patch, so the hidden detail is gone from the file.

manual_steps: Decide what must be hidden by looking at every face, plate, screen and document in the image.
Check the exported file at 100 % and strip its metadata.
